title: The Pawnbroker of the Frozen Falls
story: Behind the frozen waterfall, Driftlemaw has hung the village's storm-warning bell among his icicles and priced it at 60 amber drams. Mr 6 empties his pack: 7 moonstone shards worth 4.25 drams each, and 12 glow-snail lanterns worth 1.5 drams each. The pawnbroker taps the ice and smirks, certain the little six can't count fast enough to argue.
question: How many more drams does Mr 6 still need to buy back the bell?
solution: The moonstone shards are worth 7 × 4.25 = 29.75 drams.
The glow-snail lanterns are worth 12 × 1.5 = 18 drams, so Mr 6 has 29.75 + 18 = 47.75 drams.
The bell costs 60, so he is short 60 − 47.75 = 12.25 drams.
praise: Adding up what Mr 6 already had was smart bookkeeping — the last step was comparing that total against the 60-dram price.
hint: Work out the value of each pile separately, add them together, and only then see how far that total falls below 60.
victory: Mr 6 announced the shortfall to the quarter-dram before Driftlemaw had finished breathing on his claws, and the pawnbroker — who adored precision more than profit — handed over the bell and asked Mr 6 to audit his icicles every spring.
imagePrompt: A glittering cave behind a frozen waterfall hung with icicles and dangling trinkets, a long-fingered frost pawnbroker guarding a brass bell while a numeral-6 knight in a blue cape lays shining shards and glowing snail lanterns on an ice counter.
